title: My Soul No More Shall Strive in Vain
description: My Soul No More Shall Strive in Vain in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Anne Steele wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 241, “Self-Consecration”. The compilers changed some of the words, and this is their version.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: My soul no more shall strive in vain, Slave to the world, and slave to sin! A no-bler toil I will sus-tain, A no-bler sat-is-fac-tion win.

lines: My soul no more shall strive in vain,
Slave to the world, and slave to sin!
A nobler toil I will sustain,
I will resolve, with all my heart,
With all my powers, to serve the Lord;
Nor from His precepts e'er depart,
Whose service is a rich reward.
O, be His service all my joy!
Till others love the blest employ,
And join in labors so divine.
O, may I never faint nor tire,
Nor, wandering, leave His sacred ways;
Great God! accept my soul's desire,
And give me strength to live Thy praise.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Anne Steele died in 1778.
credits: Words by Anne Steele (1717–1778), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
